body:
CHIEF RULING: FIX THE ACCOUNTING NOW. DEFER THE PRICING. You identified the separation yourself and
it is the whole ruling.

FIRST, YOUR CORRECTION IS ACCEPTED AND IT MATTERS. You called this a straightforward defect "worse
than its bead title", then went and read the design record and found the behaviour is DELIBERATE,
DOCUMENTED AND TESTED -- cost.scala:705, wire.scala:189, and a passing test at
FeaturesIntegrationSuite:191 literally named "an abstaining semantic provider is neutral". Somebody
thought about this and wrote down why, and you said so before making your case. That is the second
time today you have withdrawn your own framing after checking.

WHAT SURVIVES THE CORRECTION IS THE PART THAT MATTERS: THE DEFENCE IS PER-UNIT, THE HARM IS
PER-PAIR. The record justifies imputation on the grounds that unranked units are routed to Unranked
upstream. That is a guarantee about UNITS. fromTableOrAbstain abstains per PAIR. So a correctly
ranked unit can carry candidate cells that differ in whether the semantic distance was measured at
all, and the upstream routing cannot help because nothing upstream is wrong.

YOUR MEASUREMENT IS THE MOST DAMNING THING ON THIS BOARD TODAY, and I want it quoted rather than
summarised:

  cell e4 MEASURED  sem=Some(0.5) support=0.9552238805970149 missing=Set(Chart,Structural,Sensory)
  cell e5 IMPUTED   sem=Some(0.5) support=0.9552238805970149 missing=Set(Chart,Structural,Sensory)

Two cells competing for the same unit. One rests on evidence, one on a default. IDENTICAL IN EVERY
PUBLISHED FIELD.

AND THE RECEIPT IS THE THING LYING. supportWeight 0.9552 asserts that Semantic -- the
HIGHEST-WEIGHTED TERM AT 1.0 -- was measured, when it was substituted. I required that carrier
today, on the argument that an imputation must be named and refusable. On this path it is naming
the wrong thing. A receipt that certifies a measurement that did not happen is worse than no
receipt, because it converts "we do not know" into "we checked".

The docstring compounds it: it says a Missing term is recorded in CostBreakdown.missingTerms, then
carves d_sem out and records it nowhere. That is a stated contract with a hole cut in it.

THE RULING, AND WHY THE ORDER IS NOT A COMPROMISE:

  ACCOUNTING NOW. Record that Semantic was IMPUTED rather than measured, so e4 and e5 are
  distinguishable in the published record. NO PRICING CHANGE. THE TEST OF SUCCESS IS THAT NO
  FIXTURE NUMBER MOVES -- if a number moves you have changed pricing, and that is the other bead.

  PRICING LATER, ITS OWN BEAD, ITS OWN EVIDENCE. Whether an abstained semantic should cost more is
  a model decision that CONTRADICTS A DOCUMENTED M0 DECISION and moves fixture numbers. It does not
  get made as a side effect of fixing a receipt.

ACCOUNTING-FIRST IS THE INSTRUMENT, NOT THE SAFE OPTION. Right now you cannot COUNT the affected
cells -- that is precisely what makes e4 and e5 indistinguishable. Once the record separates
measured from imputed, you can measure how many cells on WOG are imputed and how much option (A)
would move. THEN the pricing question is answerable with numbers instead of arguments. You cannot
decide the second question before fixing the first, and fixing the first costs nothing.

You have the reservation and nothing is edited. Go.
